Class ParametricAnalysisCase

java.lang.Object
sysmlinjava.common.SysMLAnything
sysmlinjava.occurrences.SysMLOccurrence
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLAction
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLCalculation
sysmlinjava.actions.SysMLCase
sysmlinjava.analysis.SysMLAnalysisCase
sysmlinjava.analysis.ParametricAnalysisCase
All Implemented Interfaces:
AttributeObserver, ObservableAttribute, StateBehaviorContext
Direct Known Subclasses:
AnimatedAreaAnalysisCase, AnimatedAreaGeospatialAnalysisCase, BarChartAnalysisCase, LineChartsAnalysisCase, NeuralNetworkAnalysisCase, ObjectiveFunctionAnalysisCase, ScatterPlotAnalysisCase
public abstract class ParametricAnalysisCase extends SysMLAnalysisCase implements StateBehaviorContext, ObservableAttribute, AttributeObserver
Abstract base class for the parametric analysis case, i.e. a SysMLv2 compliant representation of the SysMLv1 constraint block.

SysML parametric analysis case base class

Extensions of the ParametricAnalysisCase class declare fields and methods that represent SysMLv1 constraint block properties and operations. These include the analysis (constraint) parameters, the binding connectors (constraint parameter ports), and the binding connector functions (constraint parameter port functions), as well as features of the SysML part (block).

ObservableAttribute and AttributeObserver interfaces

The ParametricAnalysisCase is also an ObservableAttribute as well as a AttributeObserver. That is, the parameters of the parametric analysis case may be observed by other analysis cases and/or the case may observe other analysis case's values. In either case, the observed values can be parameters of the current or other analysis cases.

Parameters

As in the SysML constraint block, the ParametricAnalysisCase includes analysis parameters. These parameters correspond to the variables used in the analysis actions specified in the analysis case. Parameter fields are instances of SysMLAttributeTypes and annotated by the @Parameter annotation.

Parameter Ports

Parameters may be "bound" to values in other blocks by the SysMLBindingConnector. The SysMLBindingConnector serves as the bound reference end used in the SysML parametric diagram to "bind" parameters to attributes of parts, ports, or other parametric analysis cases. These parameter bindings are specified by fields of the SysMLBindingConnector type and are annotated with the @BindingConnector annotation and created/initialized in the createBindingConnector() operation.

Multi-Threaded Parametric Analyses

The ParametricAnalysisCase is executable as a Java thread and capable of performing multi-threaded parametric analysis during an actual model execution or simulation. This capability is typically not available in conventional diagram-based SysML tools. However, in SysMLinJava, the parametric analysis case can leverage the multi-threaded features of the Java concurrency features and of the SysMLBindingConnector to input parameters that reside in different threads of execution to "bind" values in other parts or ports to the paramtric anslysis case's parameters in a thread-safe manner. The default configuration of the ParametricAnalysisCase is to support asynchronous analysis actions in multi-threaded parts models. If a fully synchronous (single threaded) model is used, however, then the createStateMachine operation can be overridden to set the stateMachine = Optional.empty() if desired.

    • logger

    • params

      public KeyValueMap<String, SysMLAttributeType> params
      Map of the analysis parameter IDs to the parameters. Analysis parameters are updated in the map when their "bound" attribute values change and can be retrieved from the map using the parameter IDs. All analysis params are retrieved via the parameter connectors and stored in the map as basic SysMLAttributeTypes. Therefore, parameter values retrieved from the map should (must) be cast to the correct type needed for operations on the parameters, e.g in analysis calculations. Note that the parameters could be stored to/retrieved from individual instance variables in an extended parametric analysis case instead of as the mapped variables provided by this base class. However, if stored as individual instance variables, the extended case must override and implement the retrieveParameters() operation to store the retrieved parameters into these alternate variable values, because the default retrieveParameters() operation retrieves the parameters into this map.

    • paramConnectors

      @BindingConnector public KeyValueMap<String, SysMLBindingConnector> paramConnectors
      Collection of binding connectors that bind the parameters to attributes to obtain their latest values. Map keys are the paramIDs for the parameters and the map values are the binding connectors. The paramConnectors must be created/initialized/put into the map in an override of the createBindingConnectors() operation in a SysMLPart class that has access to both this case and the attribute that is bound to it's parameter

    • currentParamID

      public Optional<String> currentParamID
      Optional identification of the current (last updated) parameter. This identifier is updated for every parameter retrieval by a binding connector and can be used by the retrieveParameters() and perform() operation to identify the currently changed parameter.

    • previousParamID

      public Optional<String> previousParamID
      Optional identification of the previous (last one before current) parameter. This identifier is updated for every parameter retrieval by a binding connector and can be used by the retrieveParameters() and perform() operation to identify the previously changed parameter (to perhaps reset objects that are dependent on its changes, etc.)

  • Method Details

    • addAttributeObserver

      public void addAttributeObserver(AttributeObserver observer)
      Overridable method that performs this parametric analysis case. This method should simply perform the analysis within its body, invoking other analysis action methods as needed. The analysis actions may also be performed by a functional interface that is assigned to the function variable. The functional interface should be declared in the extended class and the function assignment should be performed in an override of the createFunction() method in the extended class. The assigned function is then invoked by this perform action, optionally invoking other methods/actions/analyses in the case as "steps" in the analysis. An example is as follows: 
      	class MyParametricAnalysis extends ParametricAnalysisCase
	{
		&#64;AnalysisCaseAction
		&#64;Override
		protected void perform()
		{
			collectParameterValues();
			calculateResult();
			evaluateResult();
			updateAnalysisDisplay();
		}

		&#64;Action
		private void collectParameterValues()
		{
			:
		}

		&#64;Action
		private void calculateResult();
		{
			:
		}

		&#64;Action
		private void evaluateResult();
		{
			:
		}

		&#64;Action
		private void updateAnalysisDisplay();
		{
			:
		}
 }
      ---OR---

      Just create the calculation/case function to be called by inherited perform() 

      	class MyParametricAnalysis extends ParametricAnalysisCase
	{
			:

		&#64;Override
		protected void createFunction()
		{
			function = (PerformedActionFunction)() ->
			{
				collectParameterValues();
				calculateResult();
				evaluateResult();
				updateAnalysisDisplay();
			};
		}
			:
	}
      Specified by:
      addAttributeObserver in interface ObservableAttribute
      Parameters:
      observer - value observer to be added

    • notifyAttributeObservers

      public void notifyAttributeObservers()
      Description copied from interface: ObservableAttribute
      Causes all AttributeObservers in the list of observers to be notified of the change of attribute, i.e. it invokes each of the AttributeObservers attributeChanged() method.

      Note this method is provided to enable model execution. It is not part of the SysML standard. To the extent the SysML standard does not provide elements for executable modeling per se, SysMLinJava includes various model elements to enable model execution.

      Specified by:
      notifyAttributeObservers in interface ObservableAttribute

    • start

      public void start()
      Starts the parametric analysis case's state machine behavior, if a state machine is present. The operation submits an InitialEvent to the state machine's event queue to thereby start its execution thread. The state machine will execute in accordance with the states and transitions that are defined in the stateMachine.

    • stop

      public void stop()
      Stops the part's state machine-based behavior, if a state machine is present in the part. The operation simply stops the state machine execution. Note if this part's state machine is asynchronous, i.e. executes in its own thread, then this operation imposes a "hard stop" where the thread is canceled regardless of what state it's in. If the part's state machine is synchronous, this operation can only queue up a FinalEvent to the event queue, on the assumption that the state machine is capable of handling the FinalEvent at the point in which the stop() method is invoked. Therefore, if a part is synchronous and this stop method is used, it's state machine should be modeled to handle the FinalEvent accordingly.
      Specified by:
      stop in interface StateBehaviorContext
      See Also:
      • SysMLPart.stop()

    • onParameterChange

      protected void onParameterChange(String paramID)
      Overridable operation that responds to bound attribute change. This default method retrieves the changed attribute from the binding connector and stores it in the corresponding parameter. By default, the parameters are assumed to reside in the params key-value map and are updated there accordingly, but the subordinate onParameterChange() method may be overridden to update the parameter in accordance with another location and/or method as needed.
      Parameters:
      paramID - unique ID of the parameter bound attribute that was changed/updated

    • onParameterChange

      protected void onParameterChange(String paramID, SysMLAttributeType paramValue)
      Overridable operation to handle a change to an attribute that is bound to an analysis parameter. Default operation simply replaces the parameter's current value in the params map with the attribute's new value. Overrides may also or only update an other instance(s) of a binding parameter that may be declared in the analysis case.

      Note that the paramValue provided is a copy of (not a reference to) the attribute at the time the attribute was changed. This enables use of the changed attribute in multi-threaded models ensuring that the attribute used for the analysis parameter will not be changed by another thread of execution during the analysis perform() operation.

      Parameters:
      paramID - ID of the bound attribute/parameter that changed
      paramValue - new instance/copy of the bound attribute/parameter

    • createStateMachine

      protected void createStateMachine()
      Overridable operation that instantiates the analysis case state machine, if any, for this analysis case. By default, the ParametricAnalysisCase creates its state machine to be an instance of the ParametricAnalysisStateMachine. Also created is a thread pool used to "run" the state machine in its own thread.

      The ParametricAnalysisStateMachine is designed to handle SysMLChangeEvents produced by BindingConnectors whose bound parameters are updated in the same or different thread(s) from the thread of the analysis action of the analysis case. It handles the events in accordance with SysML standard parametric analysis operation.
      However, if a different state machine is needed for the ParametricAnalysisCase, this createStateMachine() operation may be overridden to assign another type of SysMLStateMachine to the constraint block's stateMachine, or to assign none at all, i.e. stateMachine = Optional.empty(). If another type of SysMLStateMachine is needed, it can be installed by assigning the stateMachine variable with the instance of the custom state machine in the overriding operation. If no state machine is needed, then the overriding operation need only be set to Optional.empty().

    • createParameters

      protected void createParameters()
      Overridable abstract operation that should create the analysis's parameters initializing them and the "put"-ing the initialized instances of each into the params map with their appropriate "key"s, i.e. their parameter IDs. An example follows: 
      
 		:
	&#64;Override
	protected void createParameters()
	{
		params = KeyValueMap.of(
			List.of("paramA", "paramB", "paramC"),
			List.of(new FirstParamType(), new NextParamType(), new LastParamType()));
	}
      Note each parameter must be a type of SysMLAttributeType as the SysMLAttributeType provides the features needed for binding of analysis parameters to attributes.
      See Also:
      • SysMLAttributeType
